sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Apalachee language' (raw wikitext, downloaded 2026-09-17); phonology tables sourced to Kimball 1987:138.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Consonant/vowel inventory after Kimball 1987; only suprasegmental remark is 'Vowels may also be elongated' (citing Kimball 1987:138); nothing on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Haas, Mary R. 1949. The Position of Apalachee in the Muskogean Family. International Journal of American Linguistics 15(2):121-127.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent and read). Only prosodic remarks: fn.15 p.123 'Long vowels are not written in the Apalachee text'; sec.6 p.126 'Long vowels are not indicated in the Apalachee forms that have come down to us.' Forms cited in a standardized segmental transliteration of the 1688 letter's Spanish spelling (fn.7 p.122).
